title: Wayfinder map: dagmar — autonomous Dagger/K8s multi-agent system
description:
## Destination

A decided, **self-bootstrapping architecture** for *dagmar*: a **Dagger-based software factory** — an open-ended system organized around a **Workflow** concept (a thin CRD referencing a Dagger Go function), of which autonomous coding agents + quality-gate are one workflow family. Built on a Dagger/Kubernetes hybrid: Go control plane + Dagger as hermetic execution & sandbox engine (dag.LLM().Loop() IS the agent loop). dagmar works on the owner's own repositories and their forks, reacting to repository events and proactively running cron-driven housekeeping. Autonomy is bounded by a strict, codebase-evolving quality gate plus multi-agent review, with full autonomy (incl. merge) as the target. Binds **os-eco** (seeds / mulch / canopy) as external runtime services via adapters. Once minimally functional, dagmar **develops itself** (dogfooding) and grows with its own capabilities.

## Notes

- **Tracker**: this map lives in **seeds (sd)** — git-native, the canonical issue tracker. GitHub holds only the code. Frontier = `sd ready`.
- **Domain**: Dagger-based software factory (autonomous software-development agents are one workflow family). **Skills**: /domain-modeling, /grilling, /research, /prototype.
- **Stack**: Go (state-of-the-art: SoC, DRY, ports/adapters/hexagonal); Dagger; Kubernetes; os-eco backing services.
- **Memory & prompts**: project expertise in **mulch** (`.mulch/`, `ml prime`); prompts **composable via canopy** (`cn`).
- **Reference**: github.com/kpenfound/greetings-api demonstrates `dag.LLM()` + `CodeWorkspace` + `.Loop()` end-to-end (mulch references mx-e05f90).
- **os-eco CLIs**: `sd` (issues), `ml`/`mulch` (memory), `cn` (prompts).
- **Communication**: spoken German; all persisted writing (map, issues, code, comments) in English.
- **Reuse first**: prefer modules from https://daggerverse.dev/ and the Dagger cookbook (https://docs.dagger.io/cookbook/).

## Frontier (open tickets)

- Workflow-CRD framework — general pipelines (task, dagmar-ff60)
- Spike: os-eco tool-wrapping (task, dagmar-e8f3)

## Decisions so far

- **Execution model — Hybrid (C)** — Go/K8s control plane + agent pods; Dagger = hermetic, cached engine for code-changing actions AND the LLM/tool sandbox.
- **Scope — own repos + forks** — not a general platform or public product.
- **os-eco — external runtime services** — seeds/mulch/canopy consumed at runtime via adapter ports; not dagmar's own code.
- **Dogfooding — self-bootstrapping** — dagmar develops itself once minimal; grows with its capabilities.
- **Language & CI — Go; Dagger CI.**
- **Tracker — seeds (sd)** — canonical; GitHub = code only.
- **Autonomy target — fully autonomous** — end state is full autonomy (incl. merge), gated by the evolving quality gate + review agents; proactive cron housekeeping.
- **Agent loop — provided by Dagger** — `dag.LLM().WithEnv(env).WithPromptFile(prompt).Loop()` on a `CodeWorkspace(source, checkable)`; dagmar orchestrates around it, does not reimplement cognition. (ref: greetings-api, mulch mx-e05f90)
- **Prompts — composable via canopy**.
- **Daggerverse reuse (research, closed)** — USE NATIVE dag.git/container/http; DEPEND sagikazarmark/go, native LLM primitive, marcosnils/k3s + sagikazarmark/helm; REUSE github.com/kpenfound/dag/github-issue.
- **LLM provider (research, closed)** — default Claude behind a provider-agnostic Go port; prompts via canopy; calls in Dagger sandbox.
- **Dagger-in-K8s (research, closed)** — engine as Helm DaemonSet; pods via `_EXPERIMENTAL_DAGGER_RUNNER_HOST=kube-pod://`; 3-layer cache + optional S3/GCS.
- **Domain model — ADRs 0001-0015** (15 decided: layered language, K8s CRD boundary, ProjectManifest, Hybrid-C topology, prompt composition, autonomy model, credentials, engine tenancy, quality-gate workflow, Go module layout, sandbox trust-zones, self-bootstrap trajectory, control-plane design, platform-project scope, per-Project identity).
- **Gate family — Phase 1 done** — `dagmar-bootstrap` + `dagmar-gate` + GitHub Actions + lefthook; GITHUB_TOKEN auth (dagmar-233c).

## Not yet specified

- How dagmar wraps `dag.LLM().Loop()` for multi-step tasks; token/cost management across loops.
- Repository interaction & workspace model (clone-per-task, branching, PR flow, multi-repo fan-out).
- os-eco adapter contracts (ports for IssueTracker/Memory/Prompts; seeds/mulch/canopy specifics).
- State & persistence (task/agent/project state; run history; mulch memory contract).
- Event & trigger model (GitHub webhooks; manual; subscription).
- Proactive housekeeping & cron scheduler (bug-discovery, auto-issue-creation, repo-health).
- Autonomy & merge policy sub-decision (conditions for auto-merge; rollback).
- Deploy, isolation, RBAC & secrets (Helm/Kustomize; pod-scoped isolation; LLM/git/os-eco credentials).

## Out of scope

- General multi-project SaaS / public product with multi-tenant auth.
- Reimplementing seeds, mulch, or canopy (external services; dagmar only adapts to them).
- Reimplementing an agent cognition loop (Dagger's `dag.LLM().Loop()` provides it).
- Writing the dagmar system itself in a language other than Go.

title: Domain model & ubiquitous language
description:
Part of dagmar-80dd

## Question
What is dagmar's ubiquitous language and core domain model? Pin the entities an autonomous agent system needs — e.g. Agent, Task, Project, Workspace, Run, Sandbox, Tool, Plan, QualityGate, ReviewAgent — and the backing-service ports (IssueTracker, Memory, Prompts). Define each term, its responsibility, and key relationships, so every later ticket speaks one vocabulary.

title: Self-bootstrap & dogfooding trajectory
description:
Part of dagmar-80dd

## Question
What is the minimal, hand-built core of dagmar that can then take over developing itself, and what is the growth trajectory? Define the bootstrap boundary (what humans build first), the first capability dagmar earns (e.g. its own CI, then housekeeping, then feature work), and how it grows with its capabilities. This fixes the MVP shape and the order the rest of the map resolves in.

title: Go module layout & hexagonal architecture
description:
Part of dagmar-80dd

## Question
What is dagmar's Go module/package layout, and how are SoC / DRY / ports-and-adapters realized? Define the clean/hexagonal structure (domain core, application services, adapters for Dagger, Kubernetes, os-eco, LLM), plus config, logging, observability, and the testing strategy. This is the skeleton all implementation lands in.

title: Quality gate & multi-agent review workflow
description:
How is autonomy made safe? Design the strict, codebase-evolving quality gate (lint, tests, static analysis, AI-review thresholds) and the multi-agent review workflow (coder agent -> review agent(s) -> gate -> delivery). Define what "delivered" means (PR? merge?), how the gate evolves with the code, and the review agents' feedback loop. This is the safety core that enables the fully-autonomous target. Originally blocked by the Domain model ticket (shared vocabulary for Agent / ReviewAgent / QualityGate).

--- UPDATE 2026-07-31 (ADR-0006, dagmar-fa45 closed): the POLICY layer is decided -- merge is deterministic (controller Dagger fn; merge tool in NO Agent) and needs TWO green lights: QualityGate.green AND ReviewAgent.approve (hard veto). This ticket now owns the WORKFLOW: the coder->review->gate->delivery flow, what "delivered" means, the gate-evolution mechanism, AND the deferred Calibration Agent (disagreement analyzer -> project-persisted review-calibration mixins). Build on ADRs 0001-0006 + CONTEXT.md.
closeReason: Resolved by ADR-0009 (quality-gate workflow family). Spun out: Workflow-CRD framework, Sandbox trust-zones, Destination update (new seeds).

title: Autonomy model — levels, authoritative entity, precedence
description: ADR to define dagmar's autonomy model: discrete autonomy levels; which entity is authoritative among Project (autonomy level) / Agent (autonomy scope) / QualityGate (autonomy/merge rules); and precedence when they conflict. Core to the fully-autonomous mandate. Distinct from the review-workflow design in dagmar-e95b (this is the policy/level decision). Surfaced by foundations review B1/C3.

title: Credentials & secret management
description: ADR for secret handling: storage (K8s Secret?), per-Project scoping (a Project must not read another's credentials), and injection into Sandbox / dag.Env(). Security-critical for a system targeting autonomy on forks. Surfaced by foundations review C2.
closeReason: Resolved by ADR-0007 (docs/adr/0007-credentials-secret-management.md): per-Project namespace scoping, 3 typed secret classes, native Secret + ESO, projected per-Run injection into Sandbox/dag.Env().

title: Engine tenancy & Run concurrency
description: Decide Engine cardinality (singleton-per-cluster shared vs per-Project), Sandbox isolation/quotas across Projects, whether concurrent Runs on one Task are allowed, and who sequences Workspace lineage. Open sub-questions of the Hybrid-C topology (ADR-0004). Surfaced by foundations review A2/C4.
closeReason: Resolved by ADR-0008 (singleton engine + kube-pod:// agent pods with pods/exec RBAC + per-Project cache-volume names; Run concurrency/Workspace lineage deferred to control-plane). Spike: docs/research/spike-engine-tenancy.md. Q3 validated empirically in kind (separate client pod reached the singleton engine via kube-pod://).

title: ProjectManifest spec v0 — path, format, checkable-source projection
description: Pin ProjectManifest concrete default path and format (e.g. .dagmar/project.yaml?), and clarify the Project.checkable-source vs ProjectManifest.checkables projection (is the CR field a pointer to the manifest, or a separate default/fallback?). Surfaced by foundations review B3/B4.

title: Validate per-Project cache-volume-name isolation before multi-Project auto-merge
description: Empirically confirm Dagger isolates cache by volume name (ADR-0008 Q1 design assumption), so cross-Project cache poisoning is impossible as long as Projects use distinct cache-volume names. Validate BEFORE multi-Project autonomy (mergeAuthority==auto) is enabled. Surfaced by 2026-08-01 review B1. Method: two client pods on the singleton engine, same vs different cache-volume name, observe sharing.

title: Workflow-CRD framework (general pipelines)
description: Design the general Workflow-CRD framework spun out of ADR-0009: a Workflow is a thin CRD referencing a Dagger Go function (pipeline logic, NOT YAML steps); a Trigger references a Workflow by name; the controller invokes the Workflow's function on events. dagmar = Dagger-based software factory enabling arbitrary workflow kinds. Decide Workflow-CRD fields, Trigger->Workflow binding, controller invocation. The quality-gate family (ADR-0009) is one instance. Adds a Workflow CRD to {Project,Agent,Prompt,QualityGate,Trigger,Run}.

title: Sandbox trust-zones: hermetic LLM network segmentation
description: ADR for the execution trust-zone model spun out of ADR-0009: the LLM agent loop runs HERMETIC (no network), enforced via the Agent tool-set (no network tools); deterministic infrastructure (bootstrap, gate) has network. Trust-based network segmentation by trust level (LLM processes untrusted content -> highest isolation). Sharpens ADR-0007 (encapsulation = credential control) and the Sandbox glossary. Define the two network profiles, tool-set enforcement, and the bootstrap->LLM->gate flow.

title: Update dagmar destination: Dagger-based software factory
description: Update the dagmar wayfinder map (dagmar-80dd) Destination toward the 'Dagger-based software factory' framing surfaced in the e95b grilling (2026-08-01): CRD-driven modularity (Workflow-CRD framework) makes dagmar an open-ended software factory, of which autonomous coding agents + quality-gate are one family. Aligns Destination with the Workflow-framework direction.

title: Kubernetes control-plane design: controller topology, reconciliation & dispatch semantics
description:
Part of dagmar-80dd

## Question
What is dagmar's Kubernetes control-plane design — the controller topology, the reconciliation
model, and the dispatch/concurrency semantics that the Phase-0 lean controller (ADR-0012 §3)
grows into? This is the design home for the control-plane internals ADR-0012 explicitly deferred
out of Phase 0, and resolves the wayfinder "Kubernetes control-plane design (CRD/operator vs.
controller+workers; dispatch; concurrency)" item.

## Scope (what this seed decides)
1. **Controller topology** — one controller-runtime manager reconciling all CRDs, vs. a
   controller-per-CRD, vs. controller + worker split (wayfinder). Admission webhooks for
   validation/defaulting (ADR-0012 deferred) — yes/no at this stage, and what they validate.
2. **Reconciliation model** — the full semantics beyond the Phase-0 MVP (status conditions):
   requeue policy (on error, on not-found, on pending), error-backoff, finalizers (what cleanup
   a Run/Project deletion triggers — Sandbox teardown, cache-vol reclaim), and the status-condition
   vocabulary the controller writes back.
3. **Dispatch concurrency** — may concurrent Runs on one Task run simultaneously (ADR-0008 §5
   deferred), and if so how the controller serializes/arbitrates; the Workspace-lineage sequencing
   rule (Run-out → next Run-in; who owns the lineage pointer).
4. **agent-pod provisioning fields** — the field home for agent-pod-image and module-ref beyond
   the Phase-0 MVP reads (ADR-0012 GAP-1): Project CR spec, a ConfigMap, or the Agent CR. Version
   pinning / how the agent pod points at the right module ref on kind vs. production.
5. **State & persistence** — where task/agent/project state and run history live (wayfinder), and
   the mulch memory contract surface (read-only inside the hermetic loop per ADR-0011 §9).

## Boundary (explicitly NOT this seed — to avoid scope creep)
- **Event & trigger model** (GitHub webhooks, manual, subscription) — that is Phase 3 autonomy
  (ADR-0012 §5), a separate seed. This seed fixes the *dispatch/reconcile core*, not event sources.
- **The Phase-0 dispatch vertical itself** — that is implementation (ADR-0012 §2), already scoped.
  This seed is the *design* the Phase-0 controller grows toward; it does not block Phase 0 starting.

## Already decided (do not re-litigate)
- CRD set: {Project, Agent, Prompt, QualityGate, Trigger, Run} (ADR-0002).
- Hybrid-C topology: K8s control-plane + in-cluster singleton Dagger engine (ADR-0004).
- Agent pods are `kube-pod://` clients of the singleton engine, per-Project SA + `pods/exec` RBAC
  + distinct cache-vol names (ADR-0008). The controller provisions these per Project/Run.
- Root module hosts the CRD types (`api/v1alpha1/`) + controller (`cmd/dagmar-controller/`);
  lean controller-runtime, growing; status conditions = the Phase-0 minimal reconcile (ADR-0010 §1,
  ADR-0012 §2/§3).
- Merge is a deterministic controller function, never an LLM action; the merge tool is in no
  Agent's tool-set (ADR-0006).
- os-eco is read-local inside the hermetic loop; sync is networked outside it (ADR-0011 §9).

## Why now
Phase 0 (ADR-0012 §2) starts the controller with minimal reconcile (status conditions only) and
defers the full semantics here. Filing this seed BEFORE Phase 0 lands means the Phase-0 code is
shaped toward a decided target, not re-decided ad-hoc as the controller grows. It is the biggest
ungeseedete design gap; everything Phase 2+ (cognition, autonomy) assumes a working control plane.

title: Spike: engine-git-creds mechanism — how the singleton engine receives per-dispatch scoped git creds (Dagger v0.21.x)
Spike: os-eco tool-wrapping — manifest-declared bash commands as LLM tools (data-driven tool-registration feasibility)
Platform/project scope separation — where do platform-scope and project-scope code live? (gate-family abstraction layer)
description:
## Question

dagmar conflates two scopes in one `.dagger` module / `Dagmar` struct:
- **PLATFORM** — `Up`/`DeployEngine`/`Probe`/`ProbeNet`/`ProbeCache` (engine/cluster infra) + the root-module K8s controller/CRDs (the runtime that EXECUTES projects).
- **PROJECT** — `DagmarGate`/`DagmarBootstrap`/`DagmarSandbox` — dagmar-as-a-project's OWN gate-family conformance contract.

ADR-0009 §2 + ADR-0012 §4 establish `dagmar-bootstrap`/`dagmar-gate` as **PROJECT-scope** ("a Project must be a Dagger module exposing dagmar-bootstrap + dagmar-gate"). The violation: dagmar-the-platform calls dagmar-the-project's gate-family **directly** (shortcuit) instead of through the abstraction a normal project uses — checkout project repo → call the PROJECT's module's `dagmar-bootstrap`/`dagmar-gate`. **The abstraction layer doesn't exist yet.**

**D1 (this ticket, foundational — blocks D2/D3/D4): WHERE do platform-scope and project-scope live?** A repo/module split on top of ADR-0010's current layout — e.g. a platform module/dir (engine/controller/dispatch infra) vs a project module (`.dagmar` manifest + a thin module exposing `dagmar-bootstrap`/`dagmar-gate`). What concretely separates, and what stays shared (the `Dagmar` struct today holds both)?

**Dependents (graduate as D1 resolves):**
- **D2** — the platform→project gate-family invocation abstraction (how the platform calls a project's gate-family by module-ref; where the conformance contract is enforced).
- **D3** — dagmar-as-a-project THROUGH the abstraction (the dogfood path = the real path; what it validates).
- **D4** — toolchain-rollout (mise/bootstrap) home: project-module code (per ADR) vs a platform-provided default/convention.

**Context:** the uncommitted gate-centralization restructure (working tree) hardcodes the mise bootstrap in `.dagger/internal/workflows/bootstrap.go` — dagmar-as-a-project's bootstrap, ADR-correct as project code, but the conflation makes it read as platform-level. D1's framing determines whether that placement is right (and whether/how that restructure commits).

title: Platform manifest/CRD contract as a PUBLISHED shared library (extract from project module)
description:
## Problem

The ProjectManifest types + parser (`ProjectManifest`, `Checkable`, `ParseManifest`,
`validateWorkdir`) currently live in the PROJECT module (`dagger/dagmar-project`,
`.dagmar/internal/config/`). That is architecturally wrong: the manifest is the PLATFORM's
conformance contract (analogous to the Project CRD — a platform authority), and a user Project
must NOT own or guarantee the parsing of the platform's contract. Projects author INSTANCES
(their `.dagmar/project.yaml`); the schema + validation are platform-owned.

## Why it is (interim) in the project module

ADR-0014 GAP-1 moved the manifest with the gate-family to `.dagmar/`. Relocating it to the
platform module (`.dagger/`) as a cross-module Go dep was attempted and FAILED empirically:
Dagger loads each module in SOURCE ISOLATION, so a Go `replace dagger/dagmar => ../.dagger` (or
ANY relative-replace cross-module dep between sibling modules) cannot resolve at module-load
time — the sibling dir is absent from the load context
(`/src/.dagger/go.mod: no such file or directory`). The manifest was therefore kept in the
project module as the only Dagger-loadable option, authority enforced by convention + the future
conformance probe (ADR-0014 Q4). That is NOT clean — this issue tracks the real fix.

## Fix — a PUBLISHED shared library

Extract the manifest/contract types + parser into a standalone Go module that BOTH the platform
(`.dagger`) and the project module (`.dagmar`) depend on BY VERSION (a normal published-module
`require`, NOT a relative `replace`). A versioned remote dep resolves fine under Dagger's
source-isolated module loading — only relative sibling replaces break. This makes the contract
genuinely platform-authority (the shared library IS the platform's published contract), shared
cleanly by the platform and every conforming project.

## Scope / questions

- **Library home:** a separate Go module in this repo (a subdirectory module with its own go.mod,
  versioned via git tags) vs. a dedicated repo. Decide.
- **Resolve path:** how do `.dagger` and `.dagmar` resolve it in CI without a relative replace?
  (Subdirectory module + `go get github.com/denkhaus/dagmar/manifest@<tag>` needs the tag pushed;
  or a pseudo-version from the default branch.) Prototype the resolve end-to-end in the gate
  container before committing to a layout.
- **Move:** `manifest.go` + `manifest_test.go` out of `.dagmar/internal/config/` into the shared
  library; both modules `require` it; drop the project-local copy + the convention-only authority
  claim.
- **ADR:** update ADR-0014 GAP-1 + the manifest.go/doc.go scope notes to point at the shared
  library as the resolution (this issue's id).

## Non-goals

- Re-opening ADR-0014's module-boundary decision (Q1–Q6 stand). This refines GAP-1's manifest
  ownership only.
- Other cross-module shared types — `OsEcoConfig` stays platform-internal; the manifest is the
  only contract type shared across the boundary today.

## Relates

- ADR-0014 Consequences (GAP-1) + Deferred.
- dagmar-b8c2 (platform/project scope separation — closed; refines its GAP-1 resolution).
- dagmar-80dd (wayfinder map).

title: Identity refactor to unblock D4 finalizer — per-Run-named identity (or per-Project namespace provisioning)
description:
## Problem

ADR-0013 D4 (a Project/Run finalizer that tears down provisioned identity on deletion) is blocked,
AND a related sibling-break hazard is **already live today** (not just a future-finalizer concern —
review-19 GAP-1). Today the controller provisions agent identity per-Run but **shared-named**
within a namespace (`internal/controller/run_controller.go`, `ensureAgentIdentity`):

- SA `dagmar-agent` — Run-namespace. It is **controller-owner-ref'd to its *creating* Run**
  (`ctrl.SetControllerReference`), so deleting that Run **cascades via k8s GC today**: the SA
  vanishes and every sibling Run's pods (which run as that SA) lose their identity — admission
  failures, broken exec-into-engine. **No finalizer is required for this harm.**
- Role `dagmar-agent-exec` + RoleBinding — in the **engine** namespace (cross-namespace), binding
  that SA. Cross-namespace resources CANNOT be owner-ref'd to a Run, so they **leak** on Run
  deletion (carried over from dagmar-67bc) — the future-finalizer half of the problem.

So there are TWO distinct hazards: (1) the SA owner-ref GC sibling-break (live now), and (2) the
engine-ns Role/RoleBinding cross-namespace leak (would need a finalizer). Both stem from identity
being shared-named. Additionally: per-Project namespaces are not provisioned (Runs run in the
Project's namespace, `default`), and there is no `ProjectReconciler` or
`projects/finalizers` / `projects/status` RBAC.

## Fix (scope — decide a direction)

Make agent identity safely per-Run-deletable so neither hazard holds.

1. **Per-Run-named identity** — `dagmar-agent-<run>`, `dagmar-agent-exec-<run>`; each Run owns its
   own SA (owner-ref is now safe — deleting one Run's SA affects only that Run). The engine-ns
   Role/RoleBinding are still cross-namespace (still need a finalizer to clean), but now uniquely
   named → safe to delete per-Run. Run-level finalizer. Smaller change.
2. **Per-Project namespace provisioning** — a `ProjectReconciler` creates a namespace per Project +
   the identity inside it; the finalizer is Project-level and the whole namespace tears down
   cleanly (Role/RoleBinding move into the Project ns, restructuring the kube-pod:// RBAC). Larger;
   aligns with ADR-0008's per-Project namespace direction.

**Either way:** drop or re-scope the SA controller owner-ref so its GC no longer cascades across
sibling Runs (hazard 1), AND add a finalizer that cleans the engine-ns Role/RoleBinding (hazard 2).

Once landed: realize ADR-0013 D4, close both hazards, remove the dagmar-67bc interim TODO in
`ensureAgentIdentity`, and lift the ADR-0013 §2 D4 deferral note.

## Non-goals

- The cache-vol reclaim policy (ADR-0013 D4's other deferred half — review-15 HOUSE-4) — separate.
- Re-opening ADR-0013's reconciliation model (D3 done, D5 done); this only unblocks D4.

## Relates

- ADR-0013 §2 D4 (the deferred finalizer) + the 2026-08-06 implementation-reality note.
- review-19 GAP-1 (surfaced the live SA-owner-ref GC sibling-break).
- dagmar-67bc (carried the original engine-ns Role/RoleBinding leak TODO).
- dagmar-80dd (wayfinder map).

title: Gate: authenticate mise/ubi GitHub-API calls (GITHUB_TOKEN Dagger Secret) to stop rate-limiting
description:
## Problem

The gate's bootstrapBase (.dagmar/internal/workflows/bootstrap.go) rolls out the mise.toml toolchain (dagger, lefthook, golangci-lint, nushell via ubi) inside a Dagger container that forwards NO env. ubi therefore queries api.github.com UNAUTHENTICATED (60 req/hr/IP). Each source change invalidates the bootstrapBase cache layer (the source is mounted before the mise-install exec) → ubi re-runs → after a few gate runs the IP is rate-limited (403), failing the gate — e.g. it blocked the dagmar-a1e0 Phase B push (transient, environmental, not a code issue).

## Fix

Inject GITHUB_TOKEN into the bootstrap container as a Dagger Secret (NOT a plain WithEnvVariable — that bakes the token into the cache key + exposes it):
- bootstrap.go: bootstrapBase takes an optional `githubToken *dagger.Secret`; if non-nil, `.WithSecretVariable("GITHUB_TOKEN", githubToken)`. ubi reads GITHUB_TOKEN from env automatically (no mise config) → 5000 req/hr.
- gate.go: Gate gains an optional `+optional` `githubToken *dagger.Secret` param, threaded to bootstrapBase (runCheckable).
- lefthook.yml pre-push + .github/workflows/ci.yml: `dagger call -m .dagmar dagmar-gate --source . --github-token env:GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Caller side: a gitignored `.envrc` (direnv) exports GITHUB_TOKEN (already created during dagmar-a1e0; .envrc now gitignored). dagger develop after the Gate signature change.

Optional, token nil-safe so callers without it still work (unauthenticated, as today).

## Non-goals

- Changing the gate's bootstrap-cache strategy (mounting only mise.toml, not the full source, to stop source-change invalidation) — a separate, larger optimization.

## Relates

- dagmar-a1e0 (surfaced there; the manifest load itself is unaffected — Go fetches via git, not the API).
